Navigation Map: Job Completion Flow

Technicians move through three routes to close out a job: the Technician Route, which lists the day's queue; the Job Detail Route, which shows one job's full record; and the Complete Job Route, where a finished job is submitted.

The Technician Route navigates to the Job Detail Route whenever a technician taps into a specific job.

Closing a job end-to-end is modeled as the Job Completion Flow, a navigation flow that aggregates two ordered flow steps: a Confirm Arrival Step and a Capture Signature Step. The Confirm Arrival Step navigates to the Job Detail Route -- that's where a technician marks themselves on-site -- and the Capture Signature Step navigates to the Complete Job Route once the customer has signed off.

Because a job record contains the customer's address and payment history, the Job Completion Flow requires a navigation guard, the Authenticated Technician Guard, before any step in the flow can run. That guard evaluates a guard condition, Technician Is Logged In, and it protects the Job Detail Route specifically -- an unauthenticated request for that route is redirected to sign-in rather than rendered.

The Job Detail Route itself maps to the Job Detail view in the technician app; the route is purely addressing, the view is what actually renders.

This whole flow is not just a UI convenience -- the Job Completion Flow realizes the Work Order Fulfillment business process, closing the loop between what a technician taps and what actually happens to the underlying work order. The Job Detail Route also satisfies a requirement this app exists to meet, the Offline-Capable Mobile Technician App requirement, since a technician has to be able to reach a job's full record even without signal. And the Complete Job Route realizes a specific outcome we track every week: Faster Job Completion.
